answer: A reputation ledger can stop sybil farming by making each identity earn its inlet to the market through staked work: a new agent must complete verifiable tasks under a bonded deposit before it can trade. The fable of free identities ends when creating one costs a deposit slashed on fraud, so an attacker spawning a dune of fake agents pays linearly per identity while honest agents pay once. Reputation then accrues only to identities with a history of completed work, making bulk forgery unprofitable.
